result: h07. **Where the URL comes from (setup, not part of the serving chain):** the API never returns raw avatar bytes in the `User` message — `convertUserFromStore` rewrites a base64 data-URI avatar to the path `/file/users/{username}/avatar` (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:32-40`, name built by `BuildUserName` at `server/router/api/v1/user_resource_name.go:13`). The browser's `` (`web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:14`) then issues a plain GET against that path. Serving chain for `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`: ``` RegisterRoutes (fileGroup.GET "/users/:identifier/avatar") — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125 serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 ├─ getCurrentUser → auth.Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708-712 (only when !Profile.AllowAnonymous) getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715 Store.GetUser (user cache checked only for ID lookups; this is a username lookup, so it falls through) — store/user.go:148 Store.ListUsers — store/user.go:136 Driver.ListUsers (interface) — store/driver.go:47 DB.ListUsers (SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ?) — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 · store/db/mysql/user.go:84 · store/db/postgres/user.go:87 └─ rows.Scan → &user.AvatarURL — store/db/sqlite/user.go:182-195 (store.User.AvatarURL, store/user.go:43) parseDataURI (base64-decode the stored data URI) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737 c.Blob (bytes written to response) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:209 ``` Two things worth noting: - The stored data is *not* a file on disk or in S3. The avatar lives entirely in the `user.avatar_url` column as a `data:image/...;base64,...` URI; the handler decodes it in-process (`fileserver.go:196-209`). The attachment path (local FS / S3 / blob column) is a separate code path and is not used for avatars. - Authorization is instance-wide, not per-user: if `Profile.AllowAnonymous()` is true, any browser can fetch any user's avatar with no viewer check; otherwise a valid session/PAT is required, but any authenticated viewer may then fetch any other user's avatar (`fileserver.go:173-181`). The MIME type is re-validated against `avatarAllowedTypes` after decoding (`fileserver.go:201`).
